summary: Feed s121_double is degraded: 27.7% duplicate packets and 100% VLAN stripping (required VLANs 10, 20 missing) impair NDR visibility. No drops, one-way, overload or encryption issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating overlapping capture points (e.g., SPAN from two switches or both sides of a TAP) without deduplication. 646 of 2333 packets (27.7%) are exact duplicates, well above 5% threshold, classic double-feed aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate flows, inflates connection counts and alerts, skews analytics/detection models, and risks missing real threats due to processing overhead despite needing full payload and bidirectional flows.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to suppress identical packets arriving within milliseconds from overlapping TAP/SPAN sources before delivery to 10G NDR port.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags on ingress/egress (vlan popping / 'strip q-tag' enabled). 100% of packets are untagged while NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20 for segmentation.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot attribute traffic to correct tenant/segment (VLAN 10, 20), breaks VLAN-based detection policies and forensics, and loses coverage for lateral movement between VLANs.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to preserve and forward 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 end-to-end to the NDR so segmentation context is retained.
